text.p: Tropical storm Fran is now well inland and tracking towards the north-northwest. Top winds are down to 55 mph but heavy rains continue. We expect damage due to winds, flooding and a coastal storm surge to be quite high in North Carolina. We expect damage due to flooding and mudslides to be quite high in Virginia and West Virginia and possibly in Pennsylvania. Rainfall totals will likely reach 10-14 inches in parts of North Carolina, 5-10 inches in Virginia and West Virgina and 3-7 inches in Pennsylvania. Top winds continue to decrease during today and tonight as the system moves northward.

Typhoon Sally is becoming an increasing risk to shipping east of the northern Philippines. Top winds are now 75 mph and they could reach 130 to 140 mph during the next 48-72 hours. Shipping is at risk due to strong winds and rough seas. Sally is expected to be near the coast of north Luzon in about 48 hours. Luzon may see heavy rains developing and gusty winds. There could be mudslides in the north by the end of the weekend. If the Typhoon takes a little bit further south track the impact in Luzon would be greater.

Tropical depression 8 is expected to remain fairly weak as it tracks into the eastern Caribbean during the next 24 hours. It may become a weak tropical storm as it tracks towards Puerto Rico later in the weekend. This system is mainly a slight risk to shipping and property this period, unless it strengthens more than expected.
